models_evaluated: LASSO regression models predicting RCSI on PHQ-9 and GAD-7

links.outcome: Sensitivity and specificity of complexity model under ROC-derived versus 0.5 probability cut-offs
links.effect: Similar accuracy (ROC 0.749 vs 0.5 cut-off 0.690) but large trade-offs: sensitivity .105 vs .420, specificity .964 vs .780, changing high-intensity assignment rates.
links.quote: Notably, the ROC-based and 0.5 cut-offs for the model demonstrated large trade-offs between sensitivity and specificity despite having similar accuracy statistics.

links.outcome: Accuracy of model-derived treatment intensity assignment versus clinician-assigned intensity against actual case complexity
links.effect: Both model cut-offs had higher accuracy than clinician assignment (clinician .590; 0.5 cut-off .690; ROC cut-off .749).
links.quote: Both predictive model cut-offs demonstrated higher accuracy than the clinician-assigned treatment intensities, achieving the highest accuracy (.749) using the ROC cut-off point.

links.effect: ROC: accuracy .749, sensitivity .105, specificity .964; 0.5 cut-off: accuracy .690, sensitivity .420, specificity .780.
links.quote: The predictive models exhibited large sensitivity and specificity trade-offs (which influence the rates of patient assignment to high-intensity CBT) despite having similar accuracy statistics (ROC cut-off = 0.749, 0.5 cut-off = 0.690), emphasizing the impact of cut-off choices when implementing predictive models.
